newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set new high, new records seen.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set new high, new records seen.

text.p: Polish shares set their fourth straight 33-month high in higher turnover on Friday and analysts expected new records to be hit at the beginning of the week on apparent foreign buying.
The main market's WIG index rose 286.9 points, or 1.8 percent, to 16,628.1, and turnover rose 7.5 percent to 221 million zlotys ($76.2 million) on both markets with 50 issues up, 22 down and 14 flat.

"I believe we will set new records in the next few days, at least at the beginning of the week...but it's difficult to say for how long the capital inflow will last," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria brokerage.
Some analysts said the market, which has risen 25 percent since mid-December, could be hit by a profit-taking correction later in the week.
Analysts said they saw no signals which could significantly influence market moves but said the exchange was being pushed upwards by the uptrend on world stock exchanges.
They said computer maker Optimus, which surged 10 percent after rising 86 percent since mid-December, was extending gains on good December and 1996 earnings.
In continuous trade 14 stocks rose, three fell and four were flat in a turnover of 35.5 million zlotys ($12.2 million).
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 2.2 percent in 26.1-million- zloty ($9 million) continuous trade and eased 0.6 percent in a 20-million-zloty ($6.9 million) turnover in the regular session.
